clue.text: Filmed stories getting strange, strange looks when run back

parts.note: something strange is unfamiliar, new to us

indicators.note: running film back plays it in reverse, so the word for looks is read backwards

parts.note: leers are sly or lustful looks

explanation.surface: Footage shown in reverse draws baffled looks from an audience.
explanation.walkthrough: 'when run back' reverses LEERS. The repeated 'strange' looks like a printing doubling; only one copy does any work.
explanation.definitionFit: A newsreel was a short cinema film reporting current events, so filmed news stories.

clue.text: Demanding female subject of sex-change accepts one

indicators.note: the former gentleman takes in the next piece, so it goes inside

parts.note: a woman who was formerly a man is an ex-gent, gent being a gentleman
one is the Roman numeral I

explanation.surface: A woman who has transitioned is demanding about accepting someone.
explanation.definitionFit: Exigent describes something pressing or urgent that requires much of you.

clue.text: Drunk's hogging seafood

indicators.note: the word as slurred by a drunk, the S sound becoming SH, is what the grid takes

parts.note: someone hogging things keeps them for themselves, being greedy

explanation.surface: A tipsy diner selfishly hogs the seafood platter.
explanation.walkthrough: A drunk saying 'selfish' slurs the first S into SH, producing the word for crabs and prawns.
explanation.definitionFit: Crabs, lobsters and mussels are shellfish, a staple of seafood menus.

clue.text: Hard time upset girl

indicators.note: in a down clue upset means turned upside down, so the pieces are read upwards

parts.note: H is the pencil abbreviation for hard
tide is an old word for time, as in Yuletide

explanation.surface: A rough patch has upset a young woman.
explanation.walkthrough: 'upset' turns H + TIDE into the girl's name.
explanation.definitionFit: Edith is a female first name, and crosswords freely define names by 'girl'.

clue.text: Nothing's best as a romantic notion

parts.note: love means nothing or zero in tennis scoring
to best is to beat, so being best is to conquer all comers

explanation.surface: A cynic remarks that nothing is better than romance.
explanation.walkthrough: Read 'Nothing's best' as 'love is supreme', a famous Latin motto (amor vincit omnia).
explanation.definitionFit: The idea that romance overcomes every obstacle is a sentimental proverb from Virgil.

clue.text: Pipe? Hitch before expression of satisfaction

parts.note: to hitch something is to hook it on
ah is a sigh of contentment

explanation.surface: A smoker sighs contentedly after hitching up a water pipe.
explanation.definitionFit: A hookah is an oriental water pipe for smoking tobacco.

clue.text: Hardy's first speech cut down Nelson?

indicators.note: only the opening letter of the name Hardy is wanted
the speech is shortened by losing its final letter

parts.note: an oration is a formal speech

explanation.surface: Hardy's first words are cut short as Nelson falls at Trafalgar.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cut down' drops the last N of ORATION. The surface recalls 'Kiss me, Hardy', said by the dying Admiral Nelson to his flag captain Thomas Hardy.
explanation.definitionFit: Admiral Horatio Nelson, the British naval hero, bore this first name; the question mark flags definition by example.

clue.text: Expression of surprise about publication in Irish town

indicators.note: the cry goes round the outside of the next piece

parts.note: oh is a cry of surprise
mag is short for magazine, a publication

explanation.surface: Someone gasps at a magazine article about an Irish town.
explanation.definitionFit: Omagh is the county town of Tyrone in Northern Ireland.

clue.text: Old article on one investing in American currency

parts.note: an is the indefinite article

indicators.note: to invest in something here is to go inside it, so the numeral enters the coin

parts.note: a cent is a US coin
one is the Roman numeral I

explanation.surface: An old piece in the paper about someone investing in US money.
explanation.definitionFit: Ancient means very old, belonging to the distant past.

clue.text: A show of raging in a river

parts.note: ire is anger, a display of rage

explanation.surface: Someone throws a tantrum while standing in a river.
explanation.definitionFit: The Aire is a river in Yorkshire, flowing through Leeds.

clue.text: Little new in avarice, possibly -it's a constant state

indicators.note: the letters might be arranged otherwise, so these are mixed up

parts.note: n is the short form of new

explanation.surface: A remark that greed is a fixed human condition with little new in it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'possibly' mixes N, IN and AVARICE together.
explanation.definitionFit: Invariance is the property of never changing, staying constant.

clue.text: Try something hazardous, hiding article in tom-tom?

indicators.note: the two toms close round the article, concealing it

parts.note: read as two toms: Great Tom is a famous bell, and a tom is a male cat
the is the definite article

explanation.surface: A drummer hides something inside a tom-tom drum.
explanation.walkthrough: Belling the cat comes from the fable of mice planning to put a bell on a cat: a good plan nobody dares carry out.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means undertaking a dangerous task for the common good.

clue.text: Undesirable fellow — a man the French turned back

parts.note: he is the pronoun for a man

indicators.note: the French word is read in reverse

parts.note: le is French for the

explanation.surface: An unpleasant man is snubbed by the French.
explanation.definitionFit: A heel is a contemptible, dishonourable person, a cad.

clue.text: Moral system -this not entirely evident in the City

indicators.note: the shortened word sits inside the City postcode letters

parts.note: EC is the postcode area of the City of London

indicators.note: the word is incomplete, so its last letter goes

explanation.surface: Morality is scarcely apparent among City financiers.
explanation.walkthrough: 'not entirely' trims THIS to THI. 'evident' is padding for the surface: the City's postcode letters hold the trimmed word.
explanation.definitionFit: An ethic is a set of moral principles guiding conduct.

clue.text: Noticing nothing when travelling in disguise

indicators.note: letters on the move shift position, so these are rearranged

parts.note: O is zero, nothing

explanation.surface: A traveller in disguise notices nothing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'when travelling' rearranges NOTICING; O for nothing follows.
explanation.definitionFit: Incognito means with one's true identity concealed.

clue.text: Mentions second of candidates — possibly

indicators.note: the letters could be arranged another way, so they are mixed
the letter in second place of the word candidates is taken

explanation.surface: Someone names a second contender, perhaps.
explanation.walkthrough: 'possibly' mixes MENTIONS with A, the second letter of 'candidates'; the whole clue then describes putting candidates forward.
explanation.definitionFit: To nominate is to name or put forward candidates for a post.

clue.text: Various clues about leading figure being lustful

indicators.note: the mixed letters go around the hero
various suggests a different arrangement, so the letters are mixed

parts.note: a hero is the leading figure of a story

explanation.surface: Assorted hints point to a lustful leading man.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Various' rearranges CLUES to LECUS, and 'about' wraps those letters around HERO, splitting them LEC and US.
explanation.definitionFit: Lecherous means given to excessive sexual desire, lewd.

clue.text: Large element of heredity not initially associated with both genders

parts.note: epic means on a grand scale, large

indicators.note: the first letter is dropped

parts.note: a gene is a unit of heredity

explanation.surface: A big hereditary factor is linked to both sexes.
explanation.definitionFit: Epicene means having characteristics of both sexes, or neither.

clue.text: Pop music's version of true joy

parts.note: rap is a genre of popular music

indicators.note: a version is a different form, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A pop song's take on true happiness.
explanation.definitionFit: Rapture is intense delight, ecstasy.

clue.text: Violin-maker recalled it to a degree

indicators.note: called back, so the run of words is read in reverse

parts.note: an MA is a Master of Arts degree

explanation.surface: A violin-maker remembered it fairly well.
explanation.walkthrough: 'recalled' turns IT A MA backwards; 'to' joins. The printed grid shows AMATT, but the wordplay builds AMATI.
explanation.definitionFit: Amati was the Cremona family of luthiers whose violins predate Stradivari's.

clue.text: Fought us on snow vehicle after a short time

indicators.note: the rest follows the abbreviation for time

parts.note: t is the abbreviation for time
a sled is a sledge for snow

explanation.surface: Children scrap over a sled after a short while.
explanation.definitionFit: Tussled means struggled or scuffled with someone.

clue.text: Ends in damages after front's knocked off

indicators.note: the first letter is knocked away

parts.note: maims means injures, damages

explanation.surface: A car crash damages the front end.
explanation.definitionFit: Aims are goals, the ends one strives for.

clue.text: Soldiers heading off, climbing trail

indicators.note: in a down clue climbing means read upwards, so the letters reverse
the first letter is removed

parts.note: troops are soldiers

explanation.surface: Soldiers set off up a mountain trail.
explanation.walkthrough: 'heading off' leaves ROOPS, which 'climbing' turns round.
explanation.definitionFit: Spoor is the track or scent left by an animal.

clue.text: Obesity — indication of age after tucking into drinks

indicators.note: the wrinkle goes inside the drinks

parts.note: ports are glasses of fortified wine
lines or wrinkles on the face show age

explanation.surface: Getting fat comes with age after tucking into drinks.
explanation.definitionFit: Portliness is stoutness, being fat.

clue.text: Cunning, taking shelter by railway

parts.note: lee is the sheltered side, away from the wind

explanation.surface: A wily sort hides out by the railway line.
explanation.definitionFit: Leery can mean knowing or sly, as well as wary.

clue.text: Again fill with love — perpetual struggling about that

indicators.note: the mixed letters go round the zero
a struggling word is twisted out of shape, so its letters are mixed

parts.note: love is zero in tennis, the letter O

explanation.surface: An eternal battle to fill the heart with love once more.
explanation.definitionFit: To repopulate is to stock an area with people again.

clue.text: Left in a bind -feature of word-games?

indicators.note: the letter for left goes inside

parts.note: a tie is a restriction, a bind

explanation.surface: Someone left in a jam over a word game.
explanation.definitionFit: Scrabble is played with lettered tiles, a key feature of such games.

clue.text: Statement last month about end of dispute

parts.note: Dec is December, the final month
re means about, concerning

indicators.note: only the last letter of dispute

explanation.surface: An announcement made last month on how a quarrel ends.
explanation.definitionFit: A decree is an official order or pronouncement.

clue.text: Bet a team's set apart

parts.note: to lay is to bet, as bookmakers lay odds
a side is a team

explanation.surface: A team's stake is put on one side.
explanation.definitionFit: To lay aside is to put something away for later, reserving it.
